assumptions.condition: For every \(e\in\mathbb E\) and \(v\notin\mathcal I_e\), the structural mechanism of \(v\) under \(B_e\) equals its mechanism under \(B^*\).
The two environments use the same innovation-variance vector \(\omega\).

For every ordered pair \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), \(r_1(A,B\mid S)=r_2(A,B\mid S)\) if and only if \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\), where diff-separation is evaluated on \(G_1\cup G_2\) relative to \(D(M)\).

standard.name: Bystrova--Devijver diff-faithfulness, arXiv:2606.13947v1, the named assumption following Definitions 2--4

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(M\), the joint sample law is \(P_{M,1}^{n_1}\otimes P_{M,2}^{n_2}\).
For every \(b\in\mathbb B(s_0)\), the local rescalings \(t^{-1}(\overline{\mathcal S_b}-s_0)\) converge locally in the Painleve--Kuratowski topology to \(T_b(s_0)\) as \(t\downarrow0\).

standard.name: Chernoff regularity of local constraint sets

assumptions.condition: For every \(b\in\mathbb B(s_0)\), \(\theta_b\) has a continuously differentiable extension to a neighborhood of \(s_0\).

definitions.name: Baseline-oriented difference DAG
definitions.construction: For \(M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi)\), set \(D(M)=(\mathbb V,E_D(M))\) with \(E_D(M)=\{u\to v:u\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G^*}(v),\ B_{1,uv}\neq B_{2,uv}\}\). The directions are inherited from the baseline DAG.

definitions.name: Diff-relevant path
definitions.construction: A path \(\rho\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is diff-relevant when either it contains an edge of \(D(M)\), or it contains a non-endpoint vertex having an ancestor with at least one incoming edge in \(D(M)\).

definitions.name: Conditionally diff-relevant path
definitions.construction: Given \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\), a path \(\rho\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is conditionally diff-relevant relative to \(S\) when it is not diff-relevant and at least one condition holds: \(\rho\) contains a collider having a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); \(\rho\) contains a non-collider connected by a path active given \(S\) to a vertex of \(S\setminus\rho\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); or an endpoint of \(\rho\) has an incoming edge along \(\rho\) and a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\).

definitions.name: Diff-separation
definitions.construction: For distinct \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), define \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\) to hold exactly when \(S\) blocks every diff-relevant path and every conditionally diff-relevant path relative to \(S\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\).

definitions.name: Diff-faithful invariant-noise baseline-intervention class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}=\{M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi):\text{ass:linear-structural-equations, ass:baseline-parent-containment, ass:modular-interventions, ass:independent-gaussian-innovations, ass:invariant-innovation-variances, ass:positive-innovation-variances, and ass:diff-faithfulness hold}\}\).

definitions.name: Complete equality and sepset ledger
definitions.construction: For \(s=\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma)\), record for every ordered \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and every \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\) whether \(r_1(A,B\mid S)-r_2(A,B\mid S)=0\), together with every separating set used by the population LDiffPC skeleton and collider rules; the resulting finite record is \(\mathcal L(s)\).

definitions.name: Population LDiffPC output
definitions.construction: Run the population version of BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC Algorithm 1 on \(\mathcal L(s)\): remove an adjacency when the ledger records an equality, store its sepsets, orient unshielded colliders, and exhaust Meek rules; denote the result by \(H(s)\).

definitions.name: Exact LDiffPC-compatible causal fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F(s)=\{M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}:s(M)=s,\ D(M)\text{ has exactly the skeleton of }H(s)\text{ and agrees with every orientation recorded by }H(s)\}\).

definitions.name: Ledger and completion branch stratification
definitions.construction: Enumerate the finite baseline DAG, target-set, common-order, difference-DAG, exact-ledger-sign, LDiffPC-compatible orientation, and Cholesky cases; after clearing positive principal-minor denominators, project their polynomial equality and strict-inequality systems to covariance coordinates. Index the nonempty projected cells by \(b\in\mathbb B_p\), call them \(\mathcal S_b\), and attach the rational predecessor-regression target map \(\theta_b\).

definitions.name: Zeroth- and first-order boundary limits
definitions.construction: At \(s_0\), form \(\mathbb B(s_0)\), \(T_b(s_0)\), and \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}(h+\mathbb Z_0)\); retain \(\theta_b(s_0)\) at order zero exactly when \(T_b(s_0)\) meets the acceptance body, and at order one map every point in that intersection through \(D\theta_b(s_0)\), producing \(\mathcal K_h^{(0)}\) and \(\mathcal K_h^{(1)}\).

definitions.name: Cone-aware regular-stratum product-score image
definitions.construction: Let \(m=p(p+1)/2\). At a point \(s_0\) in the relative interior of the unique branch \(b_0\), write \(y=(y_1,y_2)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^m\), \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)=\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)\times\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2)\), and \(J=D\theta_{b_0}(s_0)=(J_1,J_2)\) according to the two covariance blocks. Define \(\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\bigl(T_{b_0}(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)\bigr)\). If \(s_0\) is in the ambient interior of \(\mathcal S_{b_0}\), then \(T_{b_0}(s_0)=\mathbb R^d\), so \(\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)=J_1\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)\oplus J_2\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2)\); if additionally \(\mathcal A_{e,\gamma}(y_e)=y_e+E_{e,\gamma}\) for its centered covariance-score ellipsoid \(E_{e,\gamma}\), then this set equals \(Jy+J_1E_{1,\gamma}\oplus J_2E_{2,\gamma}\).

definitions.name: Same-law chain--fork family
definitions.construction:
For every integer \(p\ge3\) and every \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\) with \(a\neq0\) and \(b\neq0\), choose \(W\in\mathbb V\setminus\{X,Y\}\) and enumerate the remaining vertices as \(\mathbb V\setminus\{X,Y,W\}=\{U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3}\}\).  When \(p=3\), this list is empty and every appended equation and order relation below is vacuous.  Use coordinate order \((X,Y,W,U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3})\).  In each environment of \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\), define
\[
 X=\varepsilon_X,\qquad Y=aX+\varepsilon_Y,\qquad W=bY+\varepsilon_W,
 \qquad U_j=\varepsilon_{U_j}\quad(1\le j\le p-3),
\]
where all innovations are mutually independent centered Gaussians with variance one.  In each environment of \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\), define
\[
 Y=\eta_Y,\qquad X=\frac{a}{a^2+1}Y+\eta_X,\qquad W=bY+\eta_W,
 \qquad U_j=\eta_{U_j}\quad(1\le j\le p-3),
\]
where all innovations are mutually independent centered Gaussians, with variance vector
\[
 \bigl((a^2+1)^{-1},a^2+1,1,\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{p-3}\bigr)
\]
in coordinate order \((X,Y,W,U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3})\).  Thus every \(U_j\) is independent of \((X,Y,W)\), has no incident edge, and has the same standard-Gaussian mechanism in both environments.  Within each paired SCM take the two environment coefficient matrices and innovation-variance vectors to be identical, take the displayed DAG and coefficient matrix as \((G^*,B^*)\), and take \(\mathcal I_1=\mathcal I_2=\varnothing\).  Use common orders obtained by appending \(U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3}\) to \(X\prec Y\prec W\) for \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\) and to \(Y\prec X\prec W\) for \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\).

definitions.name: Positive invariant-noise collider family
definitions.construction: For \(p=3\), factor \(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}\) under the common orders \(X\prec W\prec Y\) and \(W\prec X\prec Y\). For either order use environment \(1\) as baseline, set \(\mathcal I_1=\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal I_2=\{Y\}\), and change only the two baseline-parent coefficients into \(Y\). Both constructions induce the same difference DAG \(X\to Y\leftarrow W\), while the invariant \(X\)--\(W\) baseline edge is oriented according to the chosen common order and is absent from the difference DAG.

definitions.name: Bounded Gaussian tangent decision problem
definitions.construction: At a point with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), analyze the bounded experiment \(\{\mathcal N(h,V_0):(b,h)\in\Lambda_R\}\) with branch target \(\eta_b(h)\), Effros-measurable randomized closed-set rules \(\delta(\mathbb Y_h,U)\), uniform coverage class \(\mathfrak D_R\), and risk \(\mathfrak R_R\); characterize possible minimizers without fixing a candidate rule or proof method.

definitions.name: Full Bystrova--Devijver anchor class
definitions.construction:
Define \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}\) to be the class of baseline-indexed paired linear acyclic SCMs \(M\) for which \(\text{ass:linear-structural-equations}\), \(\text{ass:baseline-parent-containment}\), \(\text{ass:modular-interventions}\), and \(\text{ass:diff-faithfulness}\) hold, the coordinates \((\varepsilon_{e,v})_{v\in\mathbb V}\) are mutually independent for each \(e\in\mathbb E\), and the full exogenous-vector laws are invariant across environments:
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(\varepsilon_1)=\operatorname{Law}(\varepsilon_2).
\]
No Gaussian restriction is imposed in this definition.

statements.statement: For every \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\), the population covariance coordinate \(s(M)\) generates a complete ledger \(\mathcal L(s(M))\) for which BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC Theorem 1 retains the skeleton of the typed difference DAG \(D(M)\) and records only orientations present in \(D(M)\). Consequently \(D(M)\) is compatible with \(H(s(M))\), \(M\in\mathfrak F(s(M))\), and \(\tau(M)\in\Psi(s(M))\).
statements.justification: This lemma connects the discovery guarantee to coverage of the fixed causal target.
statements.gap: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC Theorem 1 proves population recovery of the difference-DAG skeleton and sound orientations under its Definitions 2--4 and diff-faithfulness, but does not state the induced effect-fiber retention result.
statements.consumer: The finite-sample confidence theorem uses retention to cover the BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B direct-effect triple rather than a selected regression surrogate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) and put \(s=s(M)\).  Positive innovation variances and acyclicity imply that both covariance matrices represented by \(s\) are positive definite, so every partial-regression denominator occurring in \(\mathcal L(s)\) is positive.  By \(\text{def:exact-ledger}\), the ledger therefore supplies perfect equality information for every ordered pair and conditioning set.  The baseline-parent containment and modularity assumptions identify the typed difference graph used here with the difference graph to which \(\text{lem:ldiffpc-population-soundness}\) applies, while \(\text{ass:diff-faithfulness}\) supplies that result's faithfulness premise.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{skel} H(s)=\operatorname{skel}D(M)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \{u\to v:u\to v\text{ is oriented in }H(s)\}
 \subseteq E_D(M).
\]
Thus \(D(M)\) has exactly the skeleton required by \(\text{def:completion-fiber}\) and agrees with every orientation recorded by \(H(s)\).  Since membership in \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) is already given and \(s(M)=s\) by construction, all three clauses of that definition hold, so \(M\in\mathfrak F(s)\).  Finally, \(\text{def:identified-effect-set}\) gives
\[
 \tau(M)\in\{\tau(M'):M'\in\mathfrak F(s)\}
 \subseteq\overline{\{\tau(M'):M'\in\mathfrak F(s)\}}=\Psi(s).
\]
This is the claimed retention of the fixed causal target; no regression functional has been substituted for \(\tau(M)\).

statements.statement: Under the two-sample Gaussian law, \(\nu_e\widehat\Sigma_e\sim\operatorname{Wishart}_p(\Sigma_{M,e},\nu_e)\) independently over \(e\in\mathbb E\). Hence \(\Pr_M\{\boldsymbol\Sigma_M\in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}\}=1-\gamma\) for every \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) and every \(n_1,n_2>p\).
statements.justification: The exact pivotal event supplies honesty without beta-min or strong-faithfulness margins.
statements.gap: StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 gives an explicit asymptotic union-of-intervals confidence set for one scalar total effect under unknown single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian DAG structure, establishing test inversion, structure unioning, and closed-form confidence construction as prior art. WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets uses residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests in identifiable additive-error structural equation models to obtain asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and model-uncertainty effect intervals. Neither provides the exact paired unrestricted-covariance Wishart pivot needed before two-environment LDiffPC fiber projection.
statements.consumer: Analysts can calibrate the causal union at a declared finite-sample level before any ledger decision is made.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) and an environment \(e\).  Acyclicity gives a permutation in which \(I-B_e^{\mathsf T}\) is triangular with unit diagonal.  Hence it is invertible, and \(\text{ass:linear-structural-equations}\) and \(\text{ass:independent-gaussian-innovations}\) imply
\[
 Z_e=(I-B_e^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\varepsilon_e
 \sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_{M,e}),\qquad
 \Sigma_{M,e}=(I-B_e^{\mathsf T})^{-1}
          \operatorname{diag}(\omega)(I-B_e)^{-1}.
\]
The matrix is positive definite because \(\min_v\omega_v>0\).  By \(\text{ass:independent-gaussian-sampling}\), the \(n_e\) rows of the data matrix \(X_e\) are independent with this law.

Let \(H_e=I_{n_e}-n_e^{-1}{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{\mathsf T}\), and choose an orthogonal \(Q_e\) satisfying
\[
 Q_e^{\mathsf T}H_eQ_e=\operatorname{diag}(0,I_{\nu_e}).
\]
Orthogonal invariance of a centered Gaussian vector with row covariance \(I_{n_e}\) shows directly from its characteristic function that the last \(\nu_e\) rows, say \(U_{e1},\ldots,U_{e\nu_e}\), of \(Q_e^{\mathsf T}X_e\) are independent \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_{M,e})\) vectors.  Therefore
\[
 \nu_e\widehat\Sigma_e=X_e^{\mathsf T}H_eX_e
   =\sum_{j=1}^{\nu_e}U_{ej}U_{ej}^{\mathsf T}
   \sim\operatorname{Wishart}_p(\Sigma_{M,e},\nu_e),
\]
which is the defining Gaussian-sum construction of the Wishart law.  Independence of the two scatter matrices follows from independence of the two samples.

For \(S_e=\Sigma_{M,e}\), set
\[
 W_e=\Sigma_{M,e}^{-1/2}(\nu_e\widehat\Sigma_e)
                 \Sigma_{M,e}^{-1/2}.
\]
Then \(W_e\sim\operatorname{Wishart}_p(I_p,\nu_e)\), and similarity invariance of trace and determinant yields
\[
 T_{e,n}(\Sigma_{M,e})
 =\nu_e\left\{\operatorname{tr}(W_e/\nu_e)
      -\log\det(W_e/\nu_e)-p\right\}.
\]
Because \(n_e>p\), one has \(\nu_e\ge p\), so \(W_e\) is positive definite almost surely and has a density on the positive-definite cone.  To see directly that the displayed pivot has no atom, partition \(W_e=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}x&z^{\mathsf T}\\z&C\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).  Conditional on \((z,C)\), positive definiteness means \(x>z^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}z\), and the pivot is, up to a constant independent of \(x\),
\[
 x-\nu_e\log\{x-z^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}z\}.
\]
This strictly decreases and then strictly increases, so every level contains at most two values of \(x\).  Fubini's theorem and the matrix density show that every pivot level has probability zero.  Thus its distribution is continuous.  With \(a_\gamma=\sqrt{1-\gamma}\), the definition of \(q_{p,\nu_e}(a_\gamma)\) therefore gives
\[
 \Pr_M\{T_{e,n}(\Sigma_{M,e})\le q_{p,\nu_e}(a_\gamma)\}=a_\gamma.
\]
The two events are independent, and \(\text{def:covariance-region}\) is their product.  Thus
\[
 \Pr_M\{\boldsymbol\Sigma_M\in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}\}
 =a_\gamma^2=1-\gamma.
\]

statements.statement: For fixed \(p\), the graph of \(s\mapsto\Psi(s)\) over \(\Omega_p\) is a finite union of semialgebraic graphs \(\{(s,\theta_b(s)):s\in\mathcal S_b\}\), indexed by \(b\in\mathbb B_p\). Every \(\mathcal S_b\) has an explicit quantifier-free description obtained from the baseline-parent, modularity, invariant-noise, positivity, diff-faithfulness, exact-ledger, typed difference-DAG, and LDiffPC-compatibility constraints, and every coordinate of \(\theta_b\) is a rational predecessor-set regression with denominators nonzero on \(\mathcal S_b\).
statements.justification: A finite rational stratification makes discontinuous post-ledger inference mathematically tractable.
statements.gap: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC gives a discovery algorithm, StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 explicitly unions intervals over unknown single-environment equal-error-variance DAG structures, and WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets builds asymptotic causal-order confidence sets from residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests in identifiable additive-error structural equation models. None gives the finite semialgebraic branch representation of a two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset direct-effect fiber.
statements.consumer: The representation supplies the exact branch list used by the confidence union and its boundary limit law.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an order \(\pi\).  For a vertex \(v\), let \(P_\pi(v)\) be the vertices preceding \(v\), and, for a positive-definite covariance matrix \(\Sigma_e\), define the ordered regression vector and residual variance
\[
 \beta_{e,v}^{\pi}
   =\Sigma_{e,P_\pi(v),P_\pi(v)}^{-1}
      \Sigma_{e,P_\pi(v),v},\qquad
 q_{e,v}^{\pi}
   =\Sigma_{e,vv}-\Sigma_{e,v,P_\pi(v)}
      \Sigma_{e,P_\pi(v),P_\pi(v)}^{-1}
      \Sigma_{e,P_\pi(v),v}.
\]
Every principal submatrix in this display is positive definite and every Schur complement \(q_{e,v}^{\pi}\) is strictly positive.  Cramer's rule consequently makes all coordinates of \(\beta_{e,v}^{\pi}\) and \(q_{e,v}^{\pi}\) rational functions of the covariance entries, with products of positive principal minors as denominators.

Suppose first that \(M\in\mathfrak F(s)\) has common order \(\pi\).  Every predecessor of \(v\) is a function of innovations preceding \(v\), whereas \(\varepsilon_{e,v}\) is independent of all those innovations by \(\text{ass:independent-gaussian-innovations}\).  Taking covariances in the structural equation for \(v\) therefore gives the normal equations
\[
 \Sigma_{e,P_\pi(v),v}
 =\Sigma_{e,P_\pi(v),P_\pi(v)}c_{e,v},
\]
where \(c_{e,v,u}=B_{e,uv}\) for a parent \(u\) and \(c_{e,v,u}=0\) for every other predecessor.  Invertibility gives \(c_{e,v}=\beta_{e,v}^{\pi}\), and taking the residual variance gives \(\omega_v=q_{e,v}^{\pi}\).  Thus, once \((s,\pi)\) is fixed, both environment coefficient matrices and the common innovation variances are unique rational functions of \(s\).

There are finitely many choices of \(\pi\), the three DAGs \(G^*,G_1,G_2\), the target sets \(\mathcal I_1,\mathcal I_2\), a ledger truth table, and a compatible partially directed output.  Fix one such discrete choice.  Substitute the rational quantities above into the following finite list: the prescribed zero and nonzero coefficient conditions; the equalities \(q_{1,v}^{\pi}=q_{2,v}^{\pi}\); the baseline-parent and modularity equalities; every equality or disequality in the complete ledger; the equivalence required by diff-faithfulness for each of the finitely many triples \((A,B,S)\); and the skeleton and orientation checks against the deterministic LDiffPC output.  Conditions involving an unconstrained baseline coefficient can be eliminated explicitly: if some environment leaves the corresponding mechanism untargeted, set the baseline coefficient equal to that environment's rational coefficient and require equality with every other untargeted environment; if both environments target the mechanism, choose any baseline value compatible with the fixed baseline-edge case.  No continuous existential variable remains.

After multiplication by the positive principal-minor and conditional-variance denominators, each equality is polynomial.  Each disequality \(f\ne0\) is the disjoint union of the two strict polynomial inequalities \(f>0\) and \(-f>0\).  Splitting the finitely many signs produces an explicit quantifier-free semialgebraic cell \(\mathcal S_b\).  This proves both finiteness and the asserted effective description.

For the same branch, the direct coefficient is
\[
 \alpha_e=
 \begin{cases}
  (\beta_{e,Y}^{\pi})_X,&X\in P_\pi(Y),\ X\to Y\in G_e,\\
  0,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
\]
and the branch map is \(\theta_b(s)=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_1-\alpha_2)\).  Hence every coordinate is a rational predecessor-set regression with a denominator that is positive, and in particular nonzero, on \(\mathcal S_b\).

Every model in \(\mathfrak F(s)\) selects one of these branches and has target \(\theta_b(s)\) by the normal-equation calculation.  Conversely, if \(s\in\mathcal S_b\), the ordered regressions, positive Schur complements, and the baseline choices just described construct structural equations satisfying every defining condition of \(\mathfrak F(s)\).  Thus the model has covariance \(s\) and target \(\theta_b(s)\).  At a fixed \(s\) there are only finitely many branch values, so their set is already closed.  Applying \(\text{def:identified-effect-set}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{graph}(\Psi)
 =\bigcup_{b\in\mathbb B_p}
   \{(s,\theta_b(s)):s\in\mathcal S_b\},
\]
as required.

statements.statement: For every \(p\ge3\), \(n_1,n_2>p\), and \(0<\gamma<1/2\), the test-inverted union obeys \(\inf_{M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}}\Pr_M\{\tau(M)\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\}\ge1-\gamma\). The infimum permits sequences on which nonzero regression-equality, conditional-independence, and completion-separation margins converge jointly to zero. The procedure assumes neither a known ledger nor a unique order or branch, conditions on no selected LDiffPC output, and imposes no beta-min or separation margin.
statements.justification: This is the boundary-honest coverage guarantee missing from plug-in post-LDiffPC inference.
statements.gap: StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 establishes asymptotic test inversion and structure unioning for one scalar total effect under unknown single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian DAG structure; WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets gives asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and post-processed effect intervals in identifiable additive-error structural equation models; ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection Theorem 2 gives asymptotic coverage after ordinary conditional-independence discovery; and GuoWuYiu2026Price gives exact selective coverage for a selected adjustment functional after Gaussian FCI when the variance is known. None gives exact unconditional coverage for a fixed paired direct-effect triple over a two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset completion fiber.
statements.consumer: The ovarian-cancer BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B comparison can report one joint confidence union for the two direct effects and their change while retaining ledger uncertainty.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) and let
\[
 E_M=\{\boldsymbol\Sigma_M\in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}\}.
\]
By \(\text{lem:wishart-pivot}\), \(\Pr_M(E_M)=1-\gamma\).  On \(E_M\), the covariance coordinate \(s(M)\) is one of the coordinates over which \(\text{def:confidence-union}\) takes its union.  By \(\text{lem:true-completion-retention}\), the fixed causal target, rather than a selected regression surrogate, satisfies \(\tau(M)\in\Psi(s(M))\).  Consequently
\[
 E_M\subseteq
 \{\tau(M)\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\},
\]
because taking the outer closure can only enlarge the union.  It follows that
\[
 \Pr_M\{\tau(M)\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\}
 \ge \Pr_M(E_M)=1-\gamma.
\]
The calculation holds for every member of the same class \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\), so taking the infimum over \(M\) preserves the inequality.  No step conditions on a selected ledger or branch.  In particular, the argument uses no lower bound on any equality, conditional-independence, or completion-separation margin, and it remains valid along arbitrary sequences on which all such nonzero margins tend to zero jointly.

statements.statement: Let \((M_N)\) be a local model sequence with \(s(M_N)=s_0+h/\sqrt N+o(N^{-1/2})\) in a true branch \(b_0\). Under tangent-cone regularity and branch smoothness, \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\Rightarrow\mathcal K_h^{(0)}\) in the Fell topology. If \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), then \(\sqrt N(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}-\tau_0)\Rightarrow\mathcal K_h^{(1)}\) in the Fell topology. The limit is derived from the paired Gaussian covariance central limit theorem and the exact Wishart acceptance bodies; it is not assumed.
statements.justification: The random-set law describes exactly which causal branches survive under simultaneous local ledger ambiguities.
statements.gap: Geyer1994Constrained derives cone limits for constrained estimators, StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 gives an explicit asymptotic structure-unioned interval, WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets gives asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and post-processed effect intervals, and ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection gives coverage and oracle equivalence under a strong signal lower bound. None derives the jointly local branch-cone random-set law at simultaneous LDiffPC equality, conditional-independence, and completion boundaries.
statements.consumer: The limit law yields boundary-aware critical-value and width calculations for LDiffPC effect reports.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(s_N=s(M_N)\), \(\widehat s_N=\operatorname{vech}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\Sigma})\), \(m=p(p+1)/2\), \(\lambda_1=\lambda\), and \(\lambda_2=1-\lambda\).  All probability statements below are under the triangular sample law generated by \(M_N\).  The local-sequence condition gives \(s_N\to s_0\); since \(s_0\in\Omega_p\), both limiting covariance matrices \(\Sigma_{0,e}\) are positive definite.

For environment \(e\), let \(X_{ei,N}=\operatorname{vech}(Z_{ei}Z_{ei}^{\mathsf T}-\Sigma_{M_N,e})\).  Gaussian fourth moments and Isserlis' identity give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(X_{ei,N})_{AB,CD}
 =\Sigma_{M_N,e,AC}\Sigma_{M_N,e,BD}
  +\Sigma_{M_N,e,AD}\Sigma_{M_N,e,BC}
 =V(\Sigma_{M_N,e})_{AB,CD}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Because \(\Sigma_{M_N,e}\to\Sigma_{0,e}\), Gaussian moments of every fixed order are uniformly bounded.  In particular, for every \(\epsilon>0\), Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 \lVert X_{ei,N}\rVert^2
 {\bf1}\{\lVert X_{ei,N}\rVert>\epsilon\sqrt{n_e}\}
 \right]
 \le \frac{\mathbb E\lVert X_{ei,N}\rVert^4}{\epsilon^2n_e}
 \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus the Lindeberg condition in \(\text{lem:multivariate-lindeberg-feller}\) holds.  Moreover, \(\overline Z_e\overline Z_e^{\mathsf T}=O_{\mathbb P_N}(n_e^{-1})\), and replacing \(n_e^{-1}\) by \(\nu_e^{-1}\) also changes the covariance half-vector by \(O_{\mathbb P_N}(n_e^{-1})\).  These are \(o_{\mathbb P_N}(n_e^{-1/2})\) because \(n_e\to\infty\).  Independence of the two samples from \(\text{ass:independent-gaussian-sampling}\), (1)--(2), \(\text{lem:multivariate-lindeberg-feller}\), and \(n_e/N\to\lambda_e\in(0,1)\) from \(\text{ass:asymptotic-sample-balance}\) therefore imply
\[
 \sqrt N(\widehat s_N-s_N)\Rightarrow\mathbb Z_0,
 \qquad
 Y_N:=\sqrt N(\widehat s_N-s_0)
 \Rightarrow y:=h+\mathbb Z_0.
 \tag{3}
\]
The covariance in (3) is \(V_0\) by definition.  It is positive definite: for a nonzero symmetric matrix \(A\), positivity of \(\Sigma_{0,e}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_e^{\mathsf T}AZ_e)
 =2\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
   \{\Sigma_{0,e}^{1/2}A\Sigma_{0,e}^{1/2}\}^2
 \right]>0,
 \tag{4}
\]
and both \(\lambda_e\) are positive.  Hence \(y\) has a Lebesgue density on \(\mathbb R^d\).

We next derive the local form of the exact Wishart bodies.  For deterministic \(z=(z_1,z_2)\), let \(\mathcal A_N(z)\) be the set of \(u=(u_1,u_2)\) for which
\[
 S_e(u_e):=\operatorname{vech}^{-1}(s_{0,e}+u_e/\sqrt N)\succ0,
 \qquad
 T_{e,n}\{S_e(u_e);z_e\}
 \le q_{p,\nu_e}(\sqrt{1-\gamma}),quad e=1,2,
 \tag{5}
\]
where the pivot in (5) uses the sample covariance with local coordinate \(z_e\).  The realized rescaled covariance region is exactly \(\mathcal A_N(Y_N)\).

Let \(g(A)=\operatorname{tr}(A)-\log\det(A)-p\).  Taylor expansion at \(I_p\) yields
\[
 g(I_p+H)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(H^2)+O(\lVert H\rVert^3).
 \tag{6}
\]
Positive definiteness of \(s_0\), \(\nu_e/N\to\lambda_e\), and (6) give, for every compact set \(K\) of \((u_e,z_e)\),
\[
 \sup_{(u_e,z_e)\in K}
 \left|T_{e,n}\{S_e(u_e);z_e\}
 -(z_e-u_e)^{\mathsf T}V_{0,e}^{-1}(z_e-u_e)
 \right|\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{7}
\]
where \(V_{0,1}=\lambda^{-1}V(\Sigma_{0,1})\) and \(V_{0,2}=(1-\lambda)^{-1}V(\Sigma_{0,2})\).  In half-vector coordinates, the inverse of \(V(\Sigma_{0,e})\) represents the quadratic form
\[
 H\longmapsto\tfrac12
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_{0,e}^{-1}H\Sigma_{0,e}^{-1}H),
 \tag{8}
\]
which accounts for the factor \(1/2\) in (6).

At the true covariance, \(\text{lem:wishart-pivot}\), the Gaussian covariance central limit calculation (1)--(3), and (6) show that the distribution whose quantile defines \(q_{p,\nu_e}(a)\) converges to \(\chi_m^2\).  The \(\chi_m^2\) distribution function is continuous and strictly increasing at its \(a_\gamma:=\sqrt{1-\gamma}\) quantile.  Quantile convergence therefore gives
\[
 q_{p,\nu_e}(a_\gamma)\longrightarrow
 q_\infty:=q_{\chi_m^2}(a_\gamma)>0.
 \tag{9}
\]
Define
\[
 E_\gamma=prod_{e=1}^2
 \{v_e:v_e^{\mathsf T}V_{0,e}^{-1}v_e\le q_\infty\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_\gamma(z)=z+E_\gamma.
 \tag{10}
\]
By (4) and (9), \(E_\gamma\) is compact, full-dimensional, semialgebraic, and regular closed.

Apply \(\text{lem:skorokhod-representation}\) to (3) and work temporarily with versions for which \(Y_N\to y\) almost surely.  Fix one such path.  If \(u_N\in\mathcal A_N(Y_N)\) and \(u_N\to u\), then (7)--(9) imply
\[
 (y_e-u_e)^{\mathsf T}V_{0,e}^{-1}(y_e-u_e)\le q_\infty,
 \quad e=1,2,
 \qquad\text{so}\qquad
 \limsup_N\mathcal A_N(Y_N)\subseteq\mathcal A_\gamma(y).
 \tag{11}
\]
If \(K\subset\operatorname{int}\mathcal A_\gamma(y)\) is compact, continuity and compactness provide \(\delta>0\) for which both limiting quadratics in (7) are at most \(q_\infty-2\delta\) on \(K\).  Equations (7), (9), and \(Y_N\to y\) then give the erosion property
\[
 K\subseteq\mathcal A_N(Y_N)
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently large }N.
 \tag{12}
\]

The exact bodies also have a common compact bound.  Indeed, let \(a_{e1},\ldots,a_{ep}\) be the eigenvalues of \(S_e^{-1/2}\widehat\Sigma_eS_e^{-1/2}\).  The scalar function \(r(a)=a-\log a-1\) is nonnegative, vanishes only at one, and is bounded away from zero off each neighborhood of one.  By (5) and (9),
\[
 0\le\sum_{j=1}^p r(a_{ej})=O(N^{-1}).
 \tag{13}
\]
Taylor's inequality for \(r\) near one now yields \(\max_j|a_{ej}-1|=O(N^{-1/2})\), uniformly over the pivot sublevel.  Since \(Y_N\) is bounded on the fixed path and \(\Sigma_{0,e}\succ0\), the resulting Loewner inequalities between \(S_e\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_e\) imply
\[
 \sup_{u\in\mathcal A_N(Y_N)}\lVert u-Y_N\rVert=O(1).
 \tag{14}
\]
Thus (11), (12), and (14) are precisely the upper-limit, erosion, and common-compact-bound conditions in \(\text{lem:generic-ellipsoid-intersection-stability}\).

For \(b\in\mathbb B(s_0)\), define
\[
 C_{b,N}=\sqrt N(\overline{\mathcal S_b}-s_0),
 \qquad
 Q_{b,N}=\overline{C_{b,N}\cap\mathcal A_N(Y_N)},
 \qquad
 Q_b(y)=T_b(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_\gamma(y).
 \tag{15}
\]
The condition \(\text{ass:tangent-cone-regularity}\), evaluated at \(t=N^{-1/2}\), states
\[
 C_{b,N}\longrightarrow T_b(s_0)
 \tag{16}
\]
locally in the Painlev\'e--Kuratowski topology.  Each cone \(T_b(s_0)\) is semialgebraic: the scaled graph used in the definition of the tangent cone is semialgebraic after introducing the positive scale variable, closure preserves semialgebraicity, and projection preserves it by \(\text{lem:tarski-seidenberg-projection}\).  There are finitely many accessible branches by \(\text{thm:finite-branch-representation}\).  Hence the union, over accessible \(b\), of the exceptional translation sets in \(\text{lem:generic-ellipsoid-intersection-stability}\) is Lebesgue null.  Because \(y\) has a density by (4), almost surely every accessible branch is simultaneously at a stable translation.

On this probability-one event, (11)--(16) and \(\text{lem:generic-ellipsoid-intersection-stability}\) give
\[
 Q_{b,N}\longrightarrow Q_b(y)
 \tag{17}
\]
in the Fell topology, with Hausdorff convergence if \(Q_b(y)\ne\varnothing\), and with \(Q_{b,N}=\varnothing\) eventually if \(Q_b(y)=\varnothing\).  The use of the closed cell in (15) does not enlarge the eventual branch image.  Indeed, \(\mathcal S_b\) is dense in \(\overline{\mathcal S_b}\).  In the lower-limit proof of the intersection lemma, a limiting point is first approximated inside \(\operatorname{int}\mathcal A_\gamma(y)\); a closed ball around that point is contained in \(\mathcal A_N(Y_N)\) eventually by (12).  Any approximating point from \(C_{b,N}\) can therefore be perturbed within that ball into \(\sqrt N(\mathcal S_b-s_0)\).  The upper limit is unchanged because \(\mathcal S_b\subseteq\overline{\mathcal S_b}\).  Consequently (17) also holds when the left side is the closure of the rescaled intersection with \(\mathcal S_b\) itself.

If \(b\notin\mathbb B(s_0)\), then \(s_0\notin\overline{\mathcal S_b}\).  Since the latter set is closed, it misses a neighborhood of \(s_0\); (14) therefore makes its intersection with the covariance region empty for all sufficiently large \(N\).  This disposes of every inaccessible branch.

It remains to map (17) through the causal target maps.  By \(\text{thm:finite-branch-representation}\) and \(\text{def:confidence-union}\), the confidence union is the closure of the finite union of the images \(\theta_b\) over the corresponding covariance intersections.  The condition \(\text{ass:branch-smoothness}\), together with the common compact bound (14), gives uniformly over the relevant \(u\),
\[
 \theta_b(s_0+u/\sqrt N)=\theta_b(s_0)+o(1).
 \tag{18}
\]
For a nonempty limiting intersection, (17)--(18) give convergence of the branch image to \(\{\theta_b(s_0)\}\); for an empty limiting intersection, the branch is eventually absent.  Taking the finite union yields, on the Skorokhod coupling,
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\longrightarrow
 \{\theta_b(s_0):b\in\mathbb B(s_0),\ Q_b(y)\ne\varnothing\}
 =\mathcal K_h^{(0)}
 \tag{19}
\]
in the Fell topology.  Almost-sure convergence of the coupled versions implies the first asserted convergence in distribution under the original triangular laws.

Finally suppose \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\).  By the definition of \(\Gamma(s_0)\), \(\theta_b(s_0)=\tau_0\) for every accessible \(b\).  Continuous differentiability and (14) sharpen (18) to the uniform expansion
\[
 \sqrt N\{\theta_b(s_0+u/\sqrt N)-\tau_0\}
 =D\theta_b(s_0)u+o(1).
 \tag{20}
\]
Apply (17) and (20) branch by branch and again take the finite union.  This gives
\[
 \sqrt N(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}-\tau_0)
 \longrightarrow
 \bigcup_{b\in\mathbb B(s_0)}
 \{D\theta_b(s_0)u:u\in T_b(s_0)\cap
 \mathcal A_\gamma(h+\mathbb Z_0)\}
 =\mathcal K_h^{(1)}
 \tag{21}
\]
almost surely on the coupling and hence in distribution, in the Fell topology, under the original laws.  Empty limiting intersections are permitted, which is why Fell convergence, rather than only convergence on the nonempty Hausdorff hyperspace, is asserted.

statements.statement: If \(s_0\) lies in the relative interior of one branch cell and \(\mathbb B(s_0)=\{b_0\}\), then, for \(y=h+\mathbb Z_0\), \(\mathcal K_h^{(0)}=\{\theta_{b_0}(s_0)\}\) when \(T_{b_0}(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal K_h^{(0)}=\varnothing\) otherwise, while \(\mathcal K_h^{(1)}=\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\bigl(T_{b_0}(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)\bigr)\), where \(J=D\theta_{b_0}(s_0)=(J_1,J_2)\). If, in addition, \(s_0\) lies in the ambient interior of \(\mathcal S_{b_0}\), then \(T_{b_0}(s_0)=\mathbb R^d\) and \(\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)=J_1\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)\oplus J_2\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2)\); if \(\mathcal A_{e,\gamma}(y_e)=y_e+E_{e,\gamma}\), this equals \(Jy+J_1E_{1,\gamma}\oplus J_2E_{2,\gamma}\). The ambient-interior image is generally a Minkowski sum rather than a joint Wald ellipsoid. Because every branch target satisfies \(\tau_3=\tau_1-\tau_2\), \(\operatorname{rank}(J)\le2\); no rank assumption is required.
statements.justification: The reduction gives the exact regular-stratum geometry by retaining the branch tangent cone and isolates the product-score Minkowski formula as an ambient-interior corollary.
statements.gap: This is an internal special-case check rather than a novelty claim: the standard constrained delta method supplies the branchwise linearization, while the proposition records the cone-intersected score image and its ambient-interior product-score reduction.
statements.consumer: Software can evaluate the regular-stratum limit by intersecting the score body with the branch cone and, only at ambient-interior points, mapping the two environment-specific score ellipsoids separately and taking their Minkowski sum.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(y=h+\mathbb Z_0\) and write \(T=T_{b_0}(s_0)\).  Since \(\mathbb B(s_0)=\{b_0\}\), the definitions in \(\text{def:boundary-limit-sets}\) reduce the zeroth-order union to
\[
 \mathcal K_h^{(0)}
 =\{\theta_{b_0}(s_0):T\cap\mathcal A_\gamma(y)\ne\varnothing\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus it is the displayed singleton when the intersection is nonempty and is empty otherwise.  Under the same singleton-branch condition, the first-order definition gives, with \(J=D\theta_{b_0}(s_0)\),
\[
 \mathcal K_h^{(1)}
 =\{Ju:u\in T\cap\mathcal A_\gamma(y)\}
 =J\bigl(T\cap\mathcal A_\gamma(y)\bigr)
 =\mathcal P_\gamma(y;b_0,s_0),
 \tag{2}
\]
where the final equality is exactly \(\text{def:regular-product-score-image}\).  Equations (1)--(2) are also the singleton-branch specialization of \(\text{thm:boundary-random-set-limit}\).

If \(s_0\) lies in the ambient interior of \(\mathcal S_{b_0}\), then some open ball about \(s_0\) is contained in the cell.  Every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) is therefore a feasible first-order direction, so
\[
 T_{b_0}(s_0)=\mathbb R^d.
 \tag{3}
\]
Writing \(u=(u_1,u_2)\), \(J=(J_1,J_2)\), and using the product definition \(\mathcal A_\gamma(y)=\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)\times\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2)\), linearity gives both inclusions in
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 J\mathcal A_\gamma(y)
 &=\{J_1u_1+J_2u_2:
       u_e\in\mathcal A_{e,\gamma}(y_e),\ e=1,2\}\\
 &=J_1\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)
   \oplus J_2\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
If \(\mathcal A_{e,\gamma}(y_e)=y_e+E_{e,\gamma}\), another application of linearity yields
\[
 J\mathcal A_\gamma(y)
 =J_1y_1+J_2y_2+J_1E_{1,\gamma}\oplus J_2E_{2,\gamma}
 =Jy+J_1E_{1,\gamma}\oplus J_2E_{2,\gamma}.
 \tag{5}
\]
This is a Minkowski sum of two linear ellipsoid images; no identity makes it a joint Wald ellipsoid in general.

Finally, every branch target has the typed form
\[
 \theta_b(s)=(\alpha_1(s),\alpha_2(s),
                    \alpha_1(s)-\alpha_2(s)).
 \tag{6}
\]
Differentiating (6), which is permitted by \(\text{ass:branch-smoothness}\), shows that the third row of \(J\) is the first row minus the second.  Hence \(\operatorname{rank}(J)\le2\).  No lower-rank or full-rank premise was used in (1)--(5), proving the proposition without a rank assumption.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\ge3\) and every \((a,b)\) in the chain--fork parameter space, the construction in \(\text{def:chain-fork-witness}\) gives two models \(M^{\mathrm{ch}},M^{\mathrm{fk}}\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) with the same law pair
\[
 \bigl(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\oplus I_{p-3}),
 \mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\oplus I_{p-3})\bigr).
\]
Here \(I_0\) denotes the empty covariance block.  The models have the same empty difference DAG, the same complete equality ledger, and the same empty population LDiffPC output, but \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{ch}})=(a,a,0)\) and \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{fk}})=(0,0,0)\).  For every ordered pair of distinct vertices and every eligible conditioning set, each model satisfies diff-faithfulness.  Therefore every procedure \((D_N)\) having coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) for both models satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\}\ge1-2\gamma
\]
for every \(N\).
statements.justification: The dimension-uniform unbounded same-law family proves both fixed-separation noncontraction and infinite global worst-case expected diameter for every p at least three, distinguishing information-theoretically necessary width from conservatism of the confidence construction.
statements.gap: ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection notes that its union may be wide and leaves minimal inflation open; it does not give an exact same-law lower bound, much less a dimension-uniform infinite global expected-diameter lower bound, for a paired direct-effect triple.
statements.consumer: Practitioners receive a formal abstention certificate when a wide BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B union reflects indistinguishable causal orders rather than numerical failure; the infinite conclusion is worst-case over each unrestricted p-dimensional class, not pointwise at that application.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(p\ge3\) and \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\) with \(a\neq0\) and \(b\neq0\).  Let \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\) and \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\) be the two paired SCMs in the corrected construction \(\text{def:chain-fork-witness}\), and write \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3})\).  For \(p=3\), this is the empty tuple and \(I_{p-3}=I_0\) is the empty covariance block.  We verify the observational law, every condition defining \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\), and the confidence lower bound.

For the chain, the structural equations and mutual independence of the unit-variance innovations give, in either environment,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(X)&=1,
 &\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)&=a,
 &\operatorname{Var}(Y)&=a^2+1,\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X,W)&=ab,
 &\operatorname{Cov}(Y,W)&=b(a^2+1),
 &\operatorname{Var}(W)&=b^2(a^2+1)+1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, \(Y=a\varepsilon_X+\varepsilon_Y\) and \(W=ab\varepsilon_X+b\varepsilon_Y+\varepsilon_W\), so each displayed identity follows by bilinearity of covariance and independence.  Thus the \((X,Y,W)\) block is
\[
 \Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)=
 \begin{pmatrix}
  1&a&ab\\
  a&a^2+1&b(a^2+1)\\
  ab&b(a^2+1)&b^2(a^2+1)+1
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
With
\[
 L=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\a&1&0\\ab&b&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
direct multiplication gives \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)=LL^{\mathsf T}\).  The matrix \(L\) is invertible because it is triangular with unit diagonal.  Hence, for every nonzero \(q\in\mathbb R^3\),
\[
 q^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)q
 =\lVert L^{\mathsf T}q\rVert_2^2>0,
 \qquad
 \det\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)=(\det L)^2=1.
\]
Consequently the block is positive definite.  Each \(U_j\) is an independent standard Gaussian and is independent of \((X,Y,W)\), by the corrected construction.  The full chain covariance is therefore
\[
 \widetilde\Sigma_p(a,b)
 =\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\oplus I_{p-3},
\]
which is positive definite and has determinant one.  In particular, its centered Gaussian law has full support \(\mathbb R^p\).

For the fork, put \(c=a/(a^2+1)\).  Since \(a^2+1>0\), every displayed innovation variance is strictly positive.  Independence and the fork equations give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(Y)&=a^2+1,
 &\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)&=c(a^2+1)=a,\\
 \operatorname{Var}(X)&=c^2(a^2+1)+(a^2+1)^{-1}=1,
 &\operatorname{Cov}(Y,W)&=b(a^2+1),\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X,W)&=b\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=ab,
 &\operatorname{Var}(W)&=b^2(a^2+1)+1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus its \((X,Y,W)\) covariance is the same \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\).  Its variables \(U_j\) are again independent standard Gaussians independent of that block, so its full covariance is also \(\widetilde\Sigma_p(a,b)\).  In either construction every observed variable is a linear combination of mutually independent centered Gaussian innovations.  Therefore each environment law is \(\mathcal N(0,\widetilde\Sigma_p(a,b))\), and the two paired models have the same asserted law pair.

We next check membership in \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) from \(\text{def:boundary-model-class}\).  The chain graph has only \(X\to Y\to W\), the fork graph has only \(Y\to X\) and \(Y\to W\), and no edge is incident to any \(U_j\).  The common orders declared in \(\text{def:chain-fork-witness}\) are topological orders, so both baseline graphs and both environment graphs are acyclic.  The displayed equations are exactly the linear structural equations in \(\text{ass:linear-structural-equations}\).  In each paired model the baseline graph and coefficient matrix equal the common environment graph and coefficient matrix, so \(\operatorname{Pa}_{G_e}(v)=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^*}(v)\) for every \(e\) and \(v\), which proves \(\text{ass:baseline-parent-containment}\).  Since \(\mathcal I_1=\mathcal I_2=\varnothing\) and every environment mechanism equals its baseline mechanism, \(\text{ass:modular-interventions}\) holds.  Mutual independence and the displayed Gaussian innovation laws prove \(\text{ass:independent-gaussian-innovations}\).  The two environments within each paired model use exactly the same variance vector, proving \(\text{ass:invariant-innovation-variances}\); all its entries are positive, proving \(\text{ass:positive-innovation-variances}\).

It remains to prove diff-faithfulness for all \(p\)-dimensional conditioning configurations.  In either paired model \(B_1=B_2\).  Hence \(\text{def:difference-dag}\) gives
\[
 D(M)=\varnothing.
\]
Fix arbitrary distinct ordered vertices \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and an arbitrary \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\).  Because \(D(M)\) has no edge, a path can neither contain an edge of \(D(M)\) nor contain a vertex having an ancestor with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\).  Thus no path is diff-relevant under \(\text{def:diff-relevant-path}\).  Each of the three alternatives in \(\text{def:conditionally-diff-relevant-path}\) also requires an incoming edge in \(D(M)\), so none is satisfied.  Therefore \(S\) blocks every path of either designated type, vacuously when no path exists, and \(\text{def:diff-separation}\) yields
\[
 A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S.
\]

For the regression side, the two environment covariance matrices within the paired model are equal to the same positive-definite matrix \(\widetilde\Sigma_p(a,b)\).  To justify division in \(r_e(A,B\mid S)\), let \(K=\widetilde\Sigma_p(a,b)_{SS}\).  If \(S\neq\varnothing\), then \(K\) is positive definite because extending a nonzero vector on \(S\) by zeros gives a nonzero vector in \(\mathbb R^p\); hence \(K\) is invertible.  With
\[
 v=\bigl(1,-K^{-1}\widetilde\Sigma_p(a,b)_{SB}\bigr)
\]
in coordinates \((B,S)\), positive definiteness of the corresponding principal submatrix gives
\[
 \widetilde\Sigma_{p,BB\cdot S}(a,b)
 =v^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\Sigma_p(a,b)_{\{B\}\cup S,\{B\}\cup S}v>0.
\]
For \(S=\varnothing\), the same conclusion is simply \(\widetilde\Sigma_{p,BB}(a,b)>0\).  Thus every partial-regression denominator is positive.  Equality of the two covariance matrices then gives, for this arbitrary triple,
\[
 r_1(A,B\mid S)=r_2(A,B\mid S).
\]
Both sides of the equivalence in \(\text{ass:diff-faithfulness}\) are true.  Since \((A,B,S)\) was arbitrary, diff-faithfulness holds for every ordered pair and eligible conditioning set, including sets containing any of the isolated variables.  All conditions in \(\text{def:boundary-model-class}\) have now been verified, so
\[
 M^{\mathrm{ch}},M^{\mathrm{fk}}\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}.
\]

The equality \(B_1=B_2\) already proved that the difference DAG of each model is empty.  Moreover, the two models have exactly the same covariance coordinate, and \(\text{def:exact-ledger}\) makes \(\mathcal L(s)\) a deterministic record of that coordinate.  Hence their complete ledgers, including every stored separating set, coincide.  Within either model every cross-environment regression difference is zero by the preceding calculation, so every equality entry in this complete ledger records equality.  The hypotheses of \(\text{lem:ldiffpc-population-soundness}\) hold by the just-proved diff-faithfulness and the exact ledger.  That lemma identifies the population output skeleton with the true difference-DAG skeleton and permits only true orientations.  Since the true skeleton is empty, the population LDiffPC output is empty for both models.

In \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\), the coefficient on \(X\to Y\) is \(a\) in each environment.  In \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\), that arrow is absent, so its coefficient is zero in each environment.  The definitions of \(\alpha_e\) and \(\tau\) give
\[
 \tau(M^{\mathrm{ch}})=(a,a,0),\qquad
 \tau(M^{\mathrm{fk}})=(0,0,0),
\]
and the Euclidean distance between these points is \(\sqrt{a^2+a^2}=\sqrt2|a|\).

Finally fix any admissible sample-size pair and its total \(N\).  By \(\text{ass:independent-gaussian-sampling}\) and equality of both environment laws, the complete sample distributions under the two witnesses coincide; denote the common distribution by \(Q_N\).  Define
\[
 E_{\mathrm{ch}}=\{(a,a,0)\in D_N\},\qquad
 E_{\mathrm{fk}}=\{(0,0,0)\in D_N\}.
\]
Coverage at the two models gives \(Q_N(E_{\mathrm{ch}})\ge1-\gamma\) and \(Q_N(E_{\mathrm{fk}})\ge1-\gamma\).  The union bound therefore yields
\[
 Q_N(E_{\mathrm{ch}}\cap E_{\mathrm{fk}})
 \ge1-Q_N(E_{\mathrm{ch}}^c)-Q_N(E_{\mathrm{fk}}^c)
 \ge1-2\gamma.
\]
On this intersection, \(D_N\) contains both target points, so its extended diameter is at least \(\sqrt2|a|\).  Hence
\[
 Q_N\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\right\}\ge1-2\gamma.
\]
The argument applies to every admissible \(N\), completing the proof.

statements.statement: For \(p=3\) and \(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}\), both covariance matrices have determinant \(4277/6250=0.68432\). Exactly the common orders \(X\prec W\prec Y\) and \(W\prec X\prec Y\) yield invariant innovation variances, and both give \(1,91/100,94/125\). Under the first order the coefficients into \(Y\) are \((B_{1,XY},B_{1,WY})=(2/5,1/5)\) and \((B_{2,XY},B_{2,WY})=(-1/10,3/5)\), and the second order gives the same four coefficients. With environment \(1\) as baseline and \(\mathcal I_2=\{Y\}\), each displayed completion belongs to \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{df}}\), induces \(D(M):X\to Y\leftarrow W\), and has a complete diff-faithful ledger compatible with the same collider-oriented \(H(s)\). Every member of the three-variable completion fiber has one of these two environment-specific ordered Cholesky factorizations, although its auxiliary baseline coefficients and intervention-target labels need not equal those of the displayed representatives. Consequently \(\Psi_3(\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}))=\{(2/5,-1/10,1/2)\}\). This statement makes no embedding or fiber claim for \(p>3\).
statements.justification: The audit shows that unresolved orientation need not force a wide effect union when all accessible environment-specific factorizations agree on the direct effect.

statements.proof_tex:
Write \(S_e=\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_e\), with rows and columns ordered as \((X,W,Y)\). Direct determinant expansion gives
\[
 \det S_1
 =1+2\frac{3}{10}\frac{23}{50}\frac{8}{25}
   -\left(\frac{3}{10}\right)^2
   -\left(\frac{23}{50}\right)^2
   -\left(\frac{8}{25}\right)^2
 =\frac{4277}{6250},
\]
and
\[
 \det S_2
 =\frac{543}{500}
   -\left(\frac{57}{100}\right)^2
   -\left(\frac{3}{10}\right)^2\frac{543}{500}
   +2\frac{3}{10}\frac{2}{25}\frac{57}{100}
   -\left(\frac{2}{25}\right)^2
 =\frac{4277}{6250}.
\]
For each matrix, the leading principal minors in the displayed coordinate order are \(1\), \(91/100\), and \(4277/6250\). They are positive, so completing squares in the Gaussian quadratic form (equivalently, Sylvester's criterion) shows that both matrices are positive definite. In particular, every principal covariance matrix inverted below is nonsingular and every residual variance below is positive.

We next justify why it is enough to inspect complete ordered factorizations. The marginal covariances and the three one-variable conditional covariances are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc|ccc}
 e& S_{e,XW}&S_{e,XY}&S_{e,WY}
  &S_{e,XW\cdot Y}&S_{e,XY\cdot W}&S_{e,WY\cdot X}\\ \hline
 1&\frac3{10}&\frac{23}{50}&\frac8{25}
  &\frac{191}{1250}&\frac{91}{250}&\frac{91}{500}\\[2pt]
 2&\frac3{10}&\frac2{25}&\frac{57}{100}
  &\frac{467}{1810}&-\frac{91}{1000}&\frac{273}{500}.
\end{array}
\]
For example, \(S_{e,AB\cdot C}=S_{e,AB}-S_{e,AC}S_{e,CC}^{-1}S_{e,CB}\); all six denominators used here are positive by positive definiteness. Every displayed number is nonzero. For completeness, in a centered nonsingular Gaussian triple the conditional density of \((A,B)\) given \(C\), obtained by completing the square in the joint density, is bivariate Gaussian with off-diagonal covariance \(S_{e,AB\cdot C}\). Its density factors into an \(A\)-part and a \(B\)-part if and only if this off-diagonal entry is zero. Thus neither environment has a marginal or one-variable conditional independence.

Let \(v_1\prec v_2\prec v_3\) be a topological order of an admissible three-variable structural model and put \(P_j=\{v_1,\ldots,v_{j-1}\}\). Taking covariance between the structural equation for \(v_j\) and the predecessor vector, and using independence of its innovation from predecessor innovations, gives
\[
 b_{e,P_jv_j}=S_{e,P_jP_j}^{-1}S_{e,P_jv_j},
 \qquad
 \omega_{e,v_j}=S_{e,v_jv_j}
 -S_{e,v_jP_j}S_{e,P_jP_j}^{-1}S_{e,P_jv_j}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The inverses exist by the preceding positivity calculation. If the edge from an earlier vertex to \(v_j\) were absent, its entry in the first expression in (1) would be zero. For \(j=2\), this would force the corresponding marginal covariance to be zero. For \(j=3\), multiplying the two-predictor normal equations out shows that a zero coefficient is equivalent to the corresponding one-variable partial covariance being zero, because the remaining conditional predictor variance is positive. The preceding table excludes both possibilities. Hence every environment DAG inducing either \(S_e\) is the complete DAG for its order, and (1) uniquely determines all of its coefficients and innovation variances.

Applying (1) to the six possible orders gives the following exhaustive table. Each variance triple is listed in the order named in the first column.
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{order}&(\omega_{1,v_1},\omega_{1,v_2},\omega_{1,v_3})
             &(\omega_{2,v_1},\omega_{2,v_2},\omega_{2,v_3})\\ \hline
 XWY&(1,\frac{91}{100},\frac{94}{125})
     &(1,\frac{91}{100},\frac{94}{125})\\
 XYW&(1,\frac{1971}{2500},\frac{8554}{9855})
     &(1,\frac{2699}{2500},\frac{8554}{13495})\\
 WXY&(1,\frac{91}{100},\frac{94}{125})
     &(1,\frac{91}{100},\frac{94}{125})\\
 WYX&(1,\frac{561}{625},\frac{4277}{5610})
     &(1,\frac{7611}{10000},\frac{34216}{38055})\\
 YXW&(1,\frac{1971}{2500},\frac{8554}{9855})
     &(\frac{543}{500},\frac{2699}{2715},\frac{8554}{13495})\\
 YWX&(1,\frac{561}{625},\frac{4277}{5610})
     &(\frac{543}{500},\frac{2537}{3620},\frac{34216}{38055}).
\end{array}
\]
Because the same order labels the same vertices in both columns, equality of the two displayed triples is precisely coordinatewise innovation-variance invariance. The table therefore leaves exactly \(X\prec W\prec Y\) and \(W\prec X\prec Y\). For the first order, the invariant edge coefficient is
\[
 B_{e,XW}=\frac{S_{e,XW}}{S_{e,XX}}=\frac3{10},
\]
and for the second it is \(B_{e,WX}=3/10\). In either order the two predecessors of \(Y\) are \(X,W\), so (1) gives
\[
\begin{split}
 B_{e,XY}
 &=\frac{S_{e,XY}S_{e,WW}-S_{e,WY}S_{e,XW}}
         {S_{e,XX}S_{e,WW}-S_{e,XW}^2},\\
 B_{e,WY}
 &=\frac{S_{e,WY}S_{e,XX}-S_{e,XY}S_{e,XW}}
         {S_{e,XX}S_{e,WW}-S_{e,XW}^2}.
\end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
The common denominator in (2) is \(91/100>0\). Substitution yields
\[
 (B_{1,XY},B_{1,WY})=(\tfrac25,\tfrac15),
 \qquad
 (B_{2,XY},B_{2,WY})=(-\tfrac1{10},\tfrac35).
 \tag{3}
\]
The last innovation variance is also \(\det(S_e)/(91/100)=94/125\), agreeing with the table.

We verify the class and ledger requirements rather than inferring them from the construction. For either surviving order, take the complete ordered DAG as \(G^*=G_1=G_2\), use (2)--(3) and the invariant coefficient \(3/10\) for \(B_1,B_2\), put \(B^*=B_1\), let \(\mathcal I_1=\varnothing\), and let \(\mathcal I_2=\{Y\}\). Choose in each environment independent centered Gaussian innovations with the positive variances in the first or third row of the table. Equation (1) then proves that the induced covariance is exactly \(S_e\), so the linear structural-equation assumption holds by construction. Parent containment holds with equality. Modularity holds because the mechanisms of \(X\) and \(W\) are unchanged, while \(Y\) is the sole target. The innovation laws are independent Gaussian, their variances are positive, and the table proves cross-environment invariance. It remains only to verify diff-faithfulness.

Let \(C\) denote the third vertex in each row. Direct evaluation of the regression definition gives the complete equality ledger
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 (A,B)&(r_1(A,B\mid\varnothing),r_2(A,B\mid\varnothing))
 &(r_1(A,B\mid C),r_2(A,B\mid C))\\ \hline
 (X,W)&(\frac3{10},\frac3{10})&(\frac{191}{1122},\frac{934}{2537})\\
 (W,X)&(\frac3{10},\frac3{10})&(\frac{382}{1971},\frac{1401}{5398})\\
 (X,Y)&(\frac{23}{50},\frac{40}{543})&(\frac{455}{1122},-\frac{910}{7611})\\
 (Y,X)&(\frac{23}{50},\frac2{25})&(\frac25,-\frac1{10})\\
 (W,Y)&(\frac8{25},\frac{95}{181})&(\frac{455}{1971},\frac{1365}{2699})\\
 (Y,W)&(\frac8{25},\frac{57}{100})&(\frac15,\frac35).
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]
Every denominator in (4) is a positive marginal or conditional variance, as required by the definition of \(r_e\). Thus equality occurs exactly for the two directions of the pair \(X,W\) with empty conditioning set.

By (3), both coefficients into \(Y\) change and the coefficient on the ordered \(X\)--\(W\) edge does not. The definition of the difference DAG therefore gives
\[
 D(M)=X\longrightarrow Y\longleftarrow W.
 \tag{5}
\]
For \(X,W\) with empty conditioning set, the direct \(X\)--\(W\) path contains no difference edge and has no non-endpoint vertex, so it is not diff-relevant; none of the three triggers for conditional diff-relevance can hold when the conditioning set is empty. The other simple path is \(X\to Y\leftarrow W\). It contains difference edges, but it is blocked at the unconditioned collider \(Y\). Hence \(X\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}W\mid\varnothing\). Conditioning on \(Y\) opens that collider path, so \(X\not\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}W\mid Y\). For the pairs \(X,Y\) and \(W,Y\), the direct path is a difference edge and has no internal vertex, so it is unblocked for either allowed conditioning set. These are all ordered pairs and conditioning sets when \(p=3\). Comparison with (4) proves the required equality if and only if diff-separation equivalence, hence diff-faithfulness. All defining conditions of \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{df}}\) have now been checked.

Under the population LDiffPC construction, (4) removes precisely the \(X\)--\(W\) adjacency and records the empty separating set for that pair. It removes neither \(X\)--\(Y\) nor \(W\)--\(Y\). Thus \(X-Y-W\) is unshielded, and because \(Y\notin\varnothing\), the collider rule orients it as \(X\to Y\leftarrow W\); there is no further unoriented adjacency on which a Meek rule could act. Therefore both displayed representatives have the same complete ledger and the same collider-oriented \(H(s)\). Equations (5) and the definition of the completion fiber show that both representatives belong to \(\mathfrak F(\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}))\).

Finally, let \(\widetilde M\) be any member of this fiber. It belongs to \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{df}}\), induces \(S_1,S_2\), and has a common topological order. The nonvanishing covariance calculation above forces each of its environment DAGs to be complete. A complete acyclic graph has a unique topological order, so the order is common to the two environments. Formula (1) then makes its environment-specific coefficients and innovation variances the unique ordered Cholesky factors in the exhaustive table. Invariance restricts its order to the first or third row, and (3) therefore holds for \(\widetilde M\). This proves the asserted exhaustion at the level of environment-specific factorizations. It does not assert uniqueness of the auxiliary baseline data: for example, taking all vertices as intervention targets makes modularity vacuous and permits alternative compatible baseline coefficients without changing \(S_e\), \(D(M)\), or the environmental factorization.

Every member of the fiber consequently has
\[
 \tau(\widetilde M)
 =\left(\frac25,-\frac1{10},\frac25+\frac1{10}\right)
 =\left(\frac25,-\frac1{10},\frac12\right).
\]
The fiber is nonempty because it contains the two displayed representatives. Hence its set of effect triples is exactly this singleton, whose closure is itself. By the definition of the three-variable identified-effect set,
\[
 \Psi_3(\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}))
 =\left\{\left(\frac25,-\frac1{10},\frac12\right)\right\}.
\]
Every step used \(p=3\); no higher-dimensional embedding or fiber assertion follows.

Fix \(s_0\) with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\) and \(R\in(0,\infty)\).  Put \(K_R=\bigcup_{(b,h)\in\Lambda_R}\{\eta_b(h)\}\) and let \(\mathcal H_R\) be the compact hyperspace of closed subsets of \(K_R\), including the empty set.  If \(\varphi_h\) is the \(\mathcal N(h,V_0)\) density, then \(v_R<\infty\), the infimum defining \(v_R\) is attained, and it has the explicit semi-infinite linear-program characterization
\[
\begin{aligned}
v_R=\min_{t,Q}\quad &t\\
\text{subject to}\quad
&Q(\,\cdot\mid y)\in\mathcal P(\mathcal H_R)\text{ measurably in }y,\\
&\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
  {\bf1}\{\eta_b(h)\in C\}\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy
  \ge1-\gamma,\quad (b,h)\in\Lambda_R,\\
&\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
  \operatorname{diam}(C)\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy
  \le t,\quad (b,h)\in\Lambda_R.
\end{aligned}
\]
After the coverage-preserving and diameter-nonincreasing truncation \(C\mapsto C\cap K_R\), the attaining \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued randomized confidence rules are exactly the measurable uniform-randomizer realizations of the minimizing kernels \(Q\), up to null sets.  In particular, every unrestricted attaining rule has an \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued truncation represented by a minimizing kernel, although the unrestricted rule itself need not be supported on \(\mathcal H_R\).  This local characterization does not by itself settle finite-sample dominance: changing any proposed pullback at one fixed sample size leaves all its local asymptotic limits unchanged while it can destroy coverage or diameter dominance at that sample size.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), the accessible branch set \(\mathbb B(s_0)\) is nonempty; it is finite because \(\mathbb B_p\) is finite.  For \(b\in\mathbb B(s_0)\), define
\[
L_{b,R}=T_b(s_0)\cap\{h\in\mathbb R^d:\|h\|_2\le R\}.
\]
The tangent cone \(T_b(s_0)\) is closed by definition, and the closed radius-\(R\) Euclidean ball is compact because \(R<\infty\).  Hence \(L_{b,R}\) is compact.  The map \(\eta_b(h)=D\theta_b(s_0)h\) is linear and therefore continuous.  It follows that
\[
K_R=\bigcup_{b\in\mathbb B(s_0)}\eta_b(L_{b,R})
\]
is a finite union of compact subsets of \(\mathbb R^3\), and thus is compact.  In particular,
\[
D_R:=\operatorname{diam}(K_R)<\infty.
\]

We first justify the restriction to the compact action space \(\mathcal H_R\).  For a closed set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^3\), put \(T(C)=C\cap K_R\).  The map \(T\) is measurable from the Effros sigma-field on closed subsets of \(\mathbb R^3\) to the Borel sigma-field of \(\mathcal H_R\).  To see this directly, let \(O=K_R\cap G\), where \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^3\) is open, and define
\[
A_m=\{x\in K_R:\operatorname{dist}(x,G^c)\ge m^{-1}\},\qquad m\ge1.
\]
With \(A_1=K_R\) when \(G^c=\varnothing\), the sets \(A_m\) are compact and \(O=\bigcup_{m\ge1}A_m\).  For any compact \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^3\), closedness of \(C\) and compactness of \(A\) imply
\[
\{C:C\cap A\ne\varnothing\}
=\bigcap_{\ell\ge1}\{C:C\cap A^{1/\ell}\ne\varnothing\},
\]
where \(A^{1/\ell}\) is the open \(1/\ell\)-neighborhood of \(A\).  Consequently both
\[
\{C:T(C)\cap O\ne\varnothing\}
=\bigcup_{m\ge1}\{C:C\cap A_m\ne\varnothing\}
\]
and, for open \(O\subseteq K_R\),
\[
\{C:T(C)\subseteq O\}
=\{C:C\cap(K_R\setminus O)=\varnothing\}
\]
are Effros measurable.  The preimage of the isolated empty member of \(\mathcal H_R\) is \(\{C:C\cap K_R=\varnothing\}\), which is measurable by the same compact-hit identity.  The displayed hit and containment sets generate the Vietoris, equivalently Hausdorff, Borel sigma-field on the compact hyperspace, proving the asserted measurability.

For every \((b,h)\in\Lambda_R\), the target \(\eta_b(h)\) belongs to \(K_R\).  Therefore, pointwise in \(C\),
\[
{\bf1}\{\eta_b(h)\in T(C)\}={\bf1}\{\eta_b(h)\in C\},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}(T(C))\le\operatorname{diam}(C).
\]
Thus truncation preserves all coverage probabilities and cannot increase any expected-diameter risk.  It follows in both directions that the unrestricted infimum \(v_R\) equals the infimum over \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued rules.  By \(\text{lem:hyperspace-compactness}\), \(\mathcal H_R\) is compact and \(C\mapsto\operatorname{diam}(C)\) is continuous on it.

We next dominate all Gaussian shifts by one law.  The matrix \(V_0\) is positive definite.  Indeed, let \(c\ne0\) be a vector in half-vector coordinates, and let \(A_c\ne0\) be the corresponding symmetric coefficient matrix, with the off-diagonal entries normalized so that contraction with a symmetric matrix agrees with contraction by \(c\) in half-vector coordinates.  Expanding the defining identity
\[
V(\Sigma)_{AB,CD}=\Sigma_{AC}\Sigma_{BD}+\Sigma_{AD}\Sigma_{BC}
\]
gives
\[
c^{\mathsf T}V(\Sigma)c
=2\operatorname{tr}\!\left\{(\Sigma^{1/2}A_c\Sigma^{1/2})^2\right\}>0
\]
for every positive-definite \(\Sigma\): the symmetric matrix \(\Sigma^{1/2}A_c\Sigma^{1/2}\) is nonzero, so the trace of its square is strictly positive.  The two covariance matrices encoded by \(s_0\in\Omega_p\) are positive definite, and \(\lambda\in(0,1)\); hence the block-diagonal definition of \(V_0\) proves \(V_0\succ0\).

Let \(\varphi_0\) denote the \(\mathcal N(0,V_0)\) density and put \(\mu_0=\mathcal N(0,V_0)\).  For every \(h\in\mathbb R^d\), completing the square in the two Gaussian densities yields the continuous, strictly positive Radon--Nikodym derivative
\[
w_h(y):=\frac{\varphi_h(y)}{\varphi_0(y)}
=\exp\!\left\{h^{\mathsf T}V_0^{-1}y
-\frac12 h^{\mathsf T}V_0^{-1}h\right\},
\qquad
\int w_h\,d\mu_0=1.
\]
This is the required corrected Gaussian likelihood ratio.

Let \(\delta\) be an \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued randomized rule.  Measurability of \(\delta\), followed by integration over the independent uniform randomizer, gives the probability kernel
\[
Q(A\mid y)=\int_0^1 {\bf1}\{\delta(y,u)\in A\}\,du,
\qquad A\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H_R).
\]
Conversely, \(\text{lem:kernel-uniform-randomization}\) realizes every probability kernel from \(\mathbb R^d\) to the standard Borel space \(\mathcal H_R\) as a jointly measurable function of \((y,U)\).  Since \(w_h\varphi_0=\varphi_h\), change of measure shows that for each \(k=(b,h)\in\Lambda_R\) the coverage and risk of \(Q\) are, respectively,
\[
G_k(Q)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
 {\bf1}\{\eta_b(h)\in C\}\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy
\]
and
\[
L_k(Q)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
 \operatorname{diam}(C)\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy.
\]
Hence the feasible kernels are exactly those satisfying \(G_k(Q)\ge1-\gamma\) for every \(k\in\Lambda_R\), and the least feasible epigraph coordinate for a fixed kernel is \(\sup_{k\in\Lambda_R}L_k(Q)\).  This proves the equality between the decision problem and the displayed semi-infinite linear program, except only for attainment.  The constant rule \(C=K_R\) has coverage one and risk \(D_R\), so
\[
0\le v_R\le D_R<\infty.
\]

We now prove attainment.  For each integer \(j\ge1\), choose a feasible kernel \(Q_j\) such that
\[
\sup_{k\in\Lambda_R}L_k(Q_j)\le v_R+j^{-1},
\]
and define a probability measure on \(\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal H_R\) by
\[
\zeta_j(dy,dC)=\mu_0(dy)Q_j(dC\mid y).
\]
Every \(\zeta_j\) has first marginal \(\mu_0\), and its second coordinate belongs to compact \(\mathcal H_R\).  Given \(\epsilon>0\), choose a compact Euclidean ball \(L_\epsilon\) with \(\mu_0(L_\epsilon)>1-\epsilon\).  Then
\[
\zeta_j(L_\epsilon\times\mathcal H_R)>1-\epsilon
\]
for every \(j\), so \((\zeta_j)_{j\ge1}\) is tight.  The product is a separable complete metric space.  By \(\text{lem:prokhorov-tightness}\), a subsequence, not relabeled, converges weakly to a probability measure \(\zeta\).

For every bounded continuous \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), weak convergence and the common first marginal give
\[
\int g(y)\,\zeta(dy,dC)
=\lim_{j\to\infty}\int g(y)\,\zeta_j(dy,dC)
=\int g(y)\,\mu_0(dy).
\]
Thus the first marginal of \(\zeta\) is \(\mu_0\).  Both factors are standard Borel spaces, so \(\text{lem:standard-borel-disintegration}\) supplies a probability kernel \(Q\) satisfying
\[
\zeta(dy,dC)=\mu_0(dy)Q(dC\mid y).
\]

Fix \(k=(b,h)\in\Lambda_R\) and define
\[
F_k=\{(y,C)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal H_R:\eta_b(h)\in C\}.
\]
The set \(F_k\) is closed: membership of a fixed point is preserved under Hausdorff convergence, and the empty member is isolated.  For \(L>0\), let \(w_h^L=w_h\wedge L\).  Since \(w_h^L\) is nonnegative and continuous and \({\bf1}_{F_k}\) is upper semicontinuous, \(w_h^L{\bf1}_{F_k}\) is bounded and upper semicontinuous.  Feasibility of \(Q_j\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int w_h^L{\bf1}_{F_k}\,d\zeta_j
&=\int w_h{\bf1}_{F_k}\,d\zeta_j
  -\int(w_h-w_h^L){\bf1}_{F_k}\,d\zeta_j\\
&\ge1-\gamma-\int(w_h-w_h^L)\,d\mu_0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The upper-semicontinuous Portmanteau inequality \(\text{lem:portmanteau-usc}\) therefore yields
\[
\int w_h^L{\bf1}_{F_k}\,d\zeta
\ge\limsup_{j\to\infty}\int w_h^L{\bf1}_{F_k}\,d\zeta_j
\ge1-\gamma-\int(w_h-w_h^L)\,d\mu_0.
\]
Because \(w_h\) is nonnegative with \(\int w_h\,d\mu_0=1\),
\[
0\le\int(w_h-w_h^L)\,d\mu_0
\le\int_{\{w_h>L\}}w_h\,d\mu_0\longrightarrow0.
\]
Monotone convergence as \(L\to\infty\) now gives
\[
G_k(Q)=\int w_h{\bf1}_{F_k}\,d\zeta\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Since \(k\) was arbitrary, \(Q\) satisfies every coverage constraint.

For risk, the function
\[
(y,C)\longmapsto w_h^L(y)\operatorname{diam}(C)
\]
is bounded and continuous by \(\text{lem:hyperspace-compactness}\).  Weak convergence therefore implies
\[
\int w_h^L(y)\operatorname{diam}(C)\,d\zeta
=\lim_{j\to\infty}
 \int w_h^L(y)\operatorname{diam}(C)\,d\zeta_j.
\]
Because both \(\zeta_j\) and \(\zeta\) have first marginal \(\mu_0\), while \(0\le\operatorname{diam}(C)\le D_R\) on \(\mathcal H_R\), replacing \(w_h^L\) by \(w_h\) changes any one of these integrals by at most
\[
D_R\int(w_h-w_h^L)\,d\mu_0\longrightarrow0,
\]
uniformly in \(j\).  Hence
\[
L_k(Q)
=\lim_{j\to\infty}L_k(Q_j)
\le v_R.
\]
This holds for every \(k\in\Lambda_R\), so \(\sup_k L_k(Q)\le v_R\).  The kernel \(Q\) is feasible, and \(v_R\) is the infimum over feasible rules; therefore \(\sup_kL_k(Q)=v_R\).  This proves attainment and the exact minimum characterization in the displayed semi-infinite linear program.

By \(\text{lem:kernel-uniform-randomization}\), every minimizing kernel has a measurable realization using \(U\), and that realization is an attaining \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued rule.  Conversely, the kernel induced by any attaining \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued rule satisfies the program constraints and has epigraph value \(v_R\), so it is minimizing.  The densities \(w_h\) are everywhere strictly positive and finite, hence all Gaussian-shift laws have the same null sets as \(\mu_0\); this proves the asserted qualification up to null sets.  If an unrestricted rule attains \(v_R\), its measurable truncation \(T\circ\delta\) remains feasible and has risk at most \(v_R\).  The definition of the infimum forces equality, and the kernel induced by this truncation is therefore minimizing.

Finally, the local characterization alone cannot imply an all-sample finite-sample comparison.  Let \((\Delta_N)_{N\ge1}\) be any proposed sequence of finite-sample pullbacks and fix one sample size \(N_0\).  Replacing only \(\Delta_{N_0}\) by the constantly empty set leaves \(\Delta_N\) unchanged for every \(N>N_0\), so it leaves every local asymptotic limit unchanged, but its coverage at \(N_0\) is zero.  Alternatively, replacing only \(\Delta_{N_0}\) by the constant set \(\mathbb R^3\) again leaves all local asymptotic limits unchanged, while its diameter at \(N_0\) is \(+\infty\), destroying any finite diameter-dominance claim there.  Thus the local minimax characterization establishes neither finite-sample coverage nor finite-sample diameter dominance for an arbitrary proposed pullback.

statements.statement: Under diff-faithfulness and perfect conditional-equality information, population LDiffPC returns the true difference-DAG skeleton, and every orientation in its output is an orientation in the true difference DAG.

source.locator: Theorem 1 in Section 5 and Appendix D
source.verbatim_statement: Under Assumption 3 and assuming access to perfect conditional equality information for all pairs of variables in V, D-hat and D have the same skeleton and all orientations present in D-hat are also present in D.

statements.statement: For a triangular array of independent mean-zero Euclidean random vectors, convergence of the covariance sums together with the Lindeberg condition implies convergence of the row sums to the centered Gaussian law with the limiting covariance.

source.verbatim_statement: For each n let the row be independent random vectors with finite variances; if the Lindeberg sums tend to zero for every positive epsilon and the covariance sums tend to Sigma, then the centered row sums converge in distribution to N(0,Sigma).

attestation.note: Verified against the Cambridge publisher preview PDF, van der Vaart (1998), Proposition 2.27, printed pages 20-21; formulas and conclusion inspected directly on 2026-09-04.

statements.statement: Every coordinate projection of a semialgebraic subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space is semialgebraic.

source.verbatim_statement: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^(n+1), and let Pi be projection on the first n coordinates. Then Pi(S) is a semi-algebraic subset of R^n.

attestation.note: Verified from the Springer source-of-record PDF, Bochnak-Coste-Roy (1998), Theorem 2.2.1, page 24; retrieved through DOI 10.1007/978-3-662-03718-8 on 2026-09-04.

statements.statement: The boundary of a semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R^d\) has dimension strictly smaller than \(d\), and therefore has \(d\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero.

source.locator: Section 2.8, dimension of semialgebraic sets, especially Proposition 2.8.13
source.verbatim_statement: Let A be a semi-algebraic set. Then dim(clos(A) minus A) is strictly smaller than dim(A).

attestation.note: Verified from the Springer source-of-record PDF, Bochnak-Coste-Roy (1998), Proposition 2.8.13, page 53. Applied to the full-dimensional interior and combined with the lower-dimensional case, this gives the boundary dimension drop; lower-dimensional semialgebraic strata are Lebesgue-null.

statements.statement: If random elements of a separable complete metric space converge in distribution, then versions with the same marginal laws can be realized on one probability space so that they converge almost surely.

source.verbatim_statement: Suppose P_n converges weakly to P and P has separable support. Then there exist random elements X_n and X on a common probability space with laws P_n and P such that X_n(omega) converges to X(omega) for every omega.

attestation.note: Verified from Billingsley (1999), Theorem 6.7, printed page 70, in a publicly served full-text PDF; the run uses this on a separable complete metric space, where the limit law has separable support.

statements.statement: A tight sequence of probability measures on a separable complete metric space has a weakly convergent subsequence.

source.verbatim_statement: If a family of probability measures is tight, then it is relatively compact.

attestation.note: Verified from Billingsley (1999), Theorem 5.1, printed page 59, in the publicly served full-text PDF linked to DOI 10.1002/9780470316962.

statements.statement: If probability measures converge weakly on a metric space, then the limit integral of every bounded upper-semicontinuous function is at least the limsup of the corresponding integrals.

source.verbatim_statement: If f is bounded and upper semicontinuous, then weak convergence P_n to P implies limsup P_n f is at most P f.

attestation.note: Verified verbatim as Billingsley (1999), Exercise 2.6 immediately following Theorem 2.1, printed page 20; the exercise explicitly identifies this as the upper-semicontinuous extension containing Theorem 2.1(iii).

statements.statement: A probability measure on a product of standard Borel spaces admits a probability-kernel disintegration with respect to either marginal.

source.verbatim_statement: Let rho be a sigma-finite measure on S times T, where T is Borel. If the first marginal is sigma-finite, rho equals its first marginal tensor a probability kernel to T.

statements.statement: Every probability kernel from a measurable space to a standard Borel space is the conditional law of a jointly measurable function of the source point and an independent uniform random variable.

source.verbatim_statement: For a probability kernel mu from S to a Borel space T and a U(0,1) variable xi, there is a measurable f from S times [0,1] to T such that f(s,xi) has distribution mu(s,.) for every s.
