statements.statement: If \(K\) is a compact subset of a Euclidean space, the hyperspace \(\mathcal H(K)\) of its closed subsets, with the empty set isolated and the Hausdorff metric on nonempty members, is compact.  The extended diameter is continuous on \(\mathcal H(K)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Consider any sequence \((C_j)\) in \(\mathcal H(K)\).  If infinitely many terms are empty, that subsequence converges to the isolated empty set.  Otherwise discard finitely many terms and assume all \(C_j\) are nonempty.  Let \((x_r)_{r\ge1}\) be a countable dense subset of \(K\).  The numbers \(d(x_r,C_j)\) lie in the compact interval \([0,\operatorname{diam}(K)]\).  Successive subsequence extraction and a diagonal argument give a subsequence along which they converge for every \(r\).  Since every function \(x\mapsto d(x,C_j)\) is one-Lipschitz, a finite-net argument upgrades convergence on the dense set to uniform convergence on \(K\); call the limit \(f\).

Choose \(z_j\in C_j\).  Compactness gives a further subsequence with \(z_j\to z\in K\), and uniform convergence implies \(f(z)=0\).  Thus \(C=\{x\in K:f(x)=0\}\) is nonempty and closed.  The one-Lipschitz property gives \(f(x)\le d(x,C)\).  Conversely, choose \(z_j(x)\in C_j\) with \(\|x-z_j(x)\|=d(x,C_j)\), pass to a convergent subsequence, and use uniform convergence to see that its limit lies in \(C\); hence \(d(x,C)\le f(x)\).  Therefore \(f=d(\,cdot\,,C)\).  Uniform convergence of distance functions for nonempty compact sets is equivalent to Hausdorff convergence, since
\[
 d_H(C_j,C)=\sup_{x\in K}|d(x,C_j)-d(x,C)|.
\]
Every sequence thus has a convergent subsequence, and the metrizable hyperspace is compact.  Finally, for nonempty \(C,D\),
\[
 |\operatorname{diam}(C)-\operatorname{diam}(D)|\le2d_H(C,D).
\]
Continuity at the isolated empty set is automatic under the convention \(\operatorname{diam}(\varnothing)=0\).  This proves both assertions.

statements.statement:
The Gaussian boundary class is a subclass of the full Bystrova--Devijver anchor class:
\[
 \mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\subseteq\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}.
\]
In particular, membership in \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) entails invariance of the full exogenous distribution, not merely equality of its coordinate variances.
statements.proof_tex:
Take \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\).  By \(\text{def:boundary-model-class}\), the model satisfies \(\text{ass:linear-structural-equations}\), \(\text{ass:baseline-parent-containment}\), \(\text{ass:modular-interventions}\), and \(\text{ass:diff-faithfulness}\), which are the four shared structural conditions in \(\text{def:bystrova-devijver-anchor-class}\).  It remains to verify causal sufficiency and invariance of the entire exogenous law.

By \(\text{ass:independent-gaussian-innovations}\), for each \(e\in\mathbb E\),
\[
 \varepsilon_e\sim\mathcal N(0,\operatorname{diag}(\omega)).
\]
By \(\text{ass:positive-innovation-variances}\), every \(\omega_v\) is strictly positive, so this law has density
\[
 f_e(x)=\prod_{v\in\mathbb V}
 (2\pi\omega_v)^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{x_v^2}{2\omega_v}\right).
\]
The displayed product factorization proves that the coordinates of \(\varepsilon_e\) are mutually independent.  Thus the innovations are causally sufficient in the sense required by the anchor class.  By \(\text{ass:invariant-innovation-variances}\), the same vector \(\omega\) occurs in both environments.  The displayed density is therefore identical for \(e=1\) and \(e=2\), proving
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(\varepsilon_1)=\operatorname{Law}(\varepsilon_2).
\]
All defining conditions of \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}\) now hold, so \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}\).  Since \(M\) was arbitrary, the asserted inclusion follows.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\ge3\) and every \((a,b)\) in the chain--fork parameter space, let \((D_N)\) be a confidence procedure satisfying
\[
 \inf_{M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}}
 \Pr_M\{\tau(M)\in D_N\}\ge 1-\gamma
\]
for every \(N\).  Then, under the common sample law of the \(p\)-dimensional chain and fork witnesses in \(\text{def:chain-fork-witness}\),
\[
 \Pr\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\}\ge1-2\gamma
\]
for every \(N\).  Thus, in every dimension \(p\ge3\), the same-law noncontraction bound applies to uniform honesty over the full, not necessarily Gaussian, Bystrova--Devijver anchor class.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(p\ge3\) and nonzero \(a,b\).  By \(\text{thm:honesty-noncontraction-lower-bound}\), the corrected chain and fork witnesses are members of \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\), have the same complete sample law, and have target vectors at Euclidean distance \(\sqrt2|a|\).  The inclusion
\[
 \mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\subseteq\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}
\]
from \(\text{lem:gaussian-subclass-of-anchor}\) puts both witnesses in the full anchor class.  The displayed uniform-coverage premise therefore gives coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) at each witness.  Applying the two-model conclusion of \(\text{thm:honesty-noncontraction-lower-bound}\) under their common law gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\right\}\ge1-2\gamma
\]
for every admissible \(N\).  Neither the inclusion nor the same-law argument imposes a bound on \(|a|\), and \(p\ge3\) was arbitrary.

statements.statement:
Fix any integer \(p\ge3\), and let \(\mathcal C\) be either \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) or \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}\).  For every \(N\), every confidence procedure satisfying
\[
 \inf_{M\in\mathcal C}\Pr_M\{\tau(M)\in D_N\}\ge1-\gamma
\]
obeys
\[
 \sup_{M\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_M\!\left[\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\right]=\infty.
\]
Consequently the infimum of this worst-case expected diameter over all such globally honest procedures is infinite for every \(p\ge3\).  By contrast, for every declared bounded tangent experiment with \(R\in(0,\infty)\), \(\text{thm:local-minimax-attainment-characterization}\) gives \(v_R<\infty\) and attainment.  Thus the theory has a dimension-uniform global-unbounded versus bounded-local elbow.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(p\ge3\), an admissible total sample size \(N\), and first take \(\mathcal C=\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\).  Set \(b=1\).  For every \(a\neq0\), global honesty supplies the two coverage inequalities required by \(\text{thm:honesty-noncontraction-lower-bound}\).  Under the common sample law \(Q_{N,a}\) of the corresponding \(p\)-dimensional witnesses, that theorem gives
\[
 Q_{N,a}\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\right\}\ge1-2\gamma.
\]
For any nonnegative extended random variable \(T\) and \(t>0\), the pointwise inequality \(T\ge t\mathbf 1\{T\ge t\}\) and monotonicity of integration imply
\[
 \mathbb E[T]\ge t\Pr\{T\ge t\}.
\]
Apply this identity with \(T=\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\) and \(t=\sqrt2|a|\).  Since either witness belongs to \(\mathcal C\) and has sample law \(Q_{N,a}\),
\[
 \sup_{M\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_M\!\left[\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\right]
 \ge \sqrt2|a|(1-2\gamma).
\]
The assumption \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\) makes \(1-2\gamma>0\).  The model class places no upper bound on \(|a|\), and the witness remains positive definite for every finite \(a\), so letting \(|a|\to\infty\) proves that the supremum is \(+\infty\).

For \(\mathcal C=\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}\), the same argument invokes \(\text{thm:anchor-class-honesty-noncontraction}\), which supplies the identical tail inequality for every \(a\neq0\).  Thus every globally honest procedure has infinite worst-case expected diameter for either class.  The collection over which the infimum is taken is nonempty: the constant closed-set rule \(D_N=\mathbb R^3\) is sample-measurable and has coverage one, although its extended diameter is infinite.  Since every member of this nonempty collection has worst-case expected diameter \(+\infty\), its infimum is \(+\infty\).

Finally, for every declared bounded tangent experiment and every \(R\in(0,\infty)\), \(\text{thm:local-minimax-attainment-characterization}\) proves \(v_R<\infty\) and produces an attaining randomized confidence rule.  Combining that finite attained local value with the global conclusion above proves the asserted elbow for every \(p\ge3\).

statements.statement: Every semialgebraic set admits a finite Whitney stratification by Nash manifolds. For a Nash mapping between Nash manifolds, the set of critical values is semialgebraic and has dimension strictly smaller than the target manifold.

source.locator: Sections 2.8, 9.1, 9.6, and 9.7, dimension, Sard, and Whitney-stratification results
source.verbatim_statement: For a Nash mapping between Nash manifolds, the critical values form a semi-algebraic subset of the target of smaller dimension. Every Nash stratification of a semi-algebraic set has a finer Nash stratification satisfying Whitney conditions a and b.

attestation.note: Verified from the Springer source-of-record PDF, Bochnak-Coste-Roy (1998), Theorem 9.6.2 (page 235) and Theorem 9.7.11 (page 242), retrieved through the DOI on 2026-09-04.

statements.statement:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed and semialgebraic, and let \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be compact, full-dimensional, semialgebraic, and regular closed, meaning \(E=\overline{\operatorname{int}E}\). Outside a semialgebraic Lebesgue-null set of translations \(y\),
\[
 C\cap(y+E)=\overline{C\cap(y+\operatorname{int}E)}.
\]
At every such \(y\), put \(D=y+E\). Let \(C_n\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed sets converging locally in the Painleve--Kuratowski topology to \(C\), and let \(D_n=y_n+E_n\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). Assume \(\limsup_nD_n\subseteq D\), every compact \(K\subseteq y+\operatorname{int}E\) is contained in \(D_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and there is a compact \(K_0\) containing \(C_n\cap D_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Then \(\overline{C_n\cap D_n}\to C\cap D\) in the Fell topology, with Hausdorff convergence whenever the limiting intersection is nonempty.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(D=y+E\).  We first identify the exceptional translations.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-stratification-sard}\), choose finite Whitney stratifications of \(C\) and \(\partial E\) by Nash manifolds, say \((S_j)_j\) and \((R_\ell)_\ell\).  For every pair of strata define the Nash map
\[
 F_{j\ell}:S_j\times R_\ell\longrightarrow\mathbb R^d,
 \qquad F_{j\ell}(c,e)=c-e.
\]
The product is a Nash manifold and the displayed map is the restriction of polynomial subtraction.  Hence \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-stratification-sard}\) says that its critical-value set \(B_{j\ell}\) is semialgebraic and has dimension strictly smaller than \(d\).  It consequently has empty interior and is contained in its boundary, so \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-boundary-null}\) gives Lebesgue measure zero.  Thus
\[
 B:=\bigcup_{j,\ell}B_{j\ell}
 \tag{1}
\]
is a semialgebraic Lebesgue-null set.

Fix \(y\notin B\).  If \(x\in C\cap(y+\partial E)\), choose the unique strata containing \(x\) and \(x-y\).  Since \(y=F_{j\ell}(x,x-y)\) is a regular value, the derivative of subtraction is onto, equivalently
\[
 T_xS_j+T_{x-y}R_\ell=\mathbb R^d.
 \tag{2}
\]
Here is the local consequence of (2) that is needed below.  In Nash charts at \(x\) and \(x-y\), choose a linear complement of \(T_{x-y}R_\ell\) inside the image of \(T_xS_j\).  Solving the corresponding normal-coordinate equations (the derivative in those selected coordinates is invertible by (2)) shows that the normal projection of \(S_j-y\) contains a neighborhood of the normal coordinate of \(R_\ell\).  The Whitney local product structure, together with \(E=\overline{\operatorname{int}E}\), then supplies points
\[
 x_r\in S_j\cap(y+\operatorname{int}E),
 \qquad x_r\longrightarrow x.
 \tag{3}
\]
For completeness, if \(R_\ell\) is zero-dimensional, (2) forces \(T_xS_j=\mathbb R^d\), so \(S_j\) is locally open and (3) follows directly from regular closedness of \(E\).  Points already in \(C\cap(y+\operatorname{int}E)\) need no approximation.  Therefore
\[
 C\cap D=\overline{C\cap\operatorname{int}D}.
 \tag{4}
\]

Now put \(A_n=\overline{C_n\cap D_n}\) and \(A=C\cap D\).  To prove the upper set limit, take any subsequence, still indexed by \(n\), and points \(x_n\in A_n\) with \(x_n\to x\).  Choose \(z_n\in C_n\cap D_n\) with \(\lVert z_n-x_n\rVert\le n^{-1}\).  Local Painlev\'e--Kuratowski upper convergence of \(C_n\), and the assumed inclusion \(\limsup_nD_n\subseteq D\), imply
\[
 x=\lim_nz_n\in C\cap D=A.
 \tag{5}
\]
Thus \(\limsup_nA_n\subseteq A\).

For the lower set limit, fix \(x\in A\).  By (4), choose \(x^{(r)}\in C\cap\operatorname{int}D\) with \(x^{(r)}\to x\).  Choose \(\varepsilon_r>0\) such that
\[
 K_r:=\overline B(x^{(r)},\varepsilon_r)
 \subseteq\operatorname{int}D.
 \tag{6}
\]
Local Painlev\'e--Kuratowski lower convergence gives \(x_n^{(r)}\in C_n\) with \(x_n^{(r)}\to x^{(r)}\).  For each fixed \(r\), eventually \(x_n^{(r)}\in K_r\), while the stated erosion hypothesis applied to the compact set \(K_r\) gives \(K_r\subseteq D_n\) eventually.  Hence \(x_n^{(r)}\in C_n\cap D_n\) eventually.  A diagonal choice, first in \(n\) and then in \(r\), produces points of \(A_n\) converging to \(x\), and therefore
\[
 A\subseteq\liminf_nA_n.
 \tag{7}
\]
Equations (5)--(7) prove Painlev\'e--Kuratowski, hence Fell, convergence \(A_n\to A\).

Finally, the common-compact-bound hypothesis places every sufficiently large \(A_n\) in one compact set.  If \(A=\varnothing\) and infinitely many \(A_n\) were nonempty, compactness would produce a convergent subsequence of selected points, contradicting (5); hence \(A_n=\varnothing\) eventually.  If \(A\ne\varnothing\), upper and lower convergence inside that common compact set are equivalent to Hausdorff convergence.  This proves all assertions.

sampling_model.design: Two independent observational samples from centered positive linear-Gaussian acyclic SCMs in \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\), with baseline-parent modular interventions and invariant innovation variances.
sampling_model.units: Within environment \(e\), \(Z_{e1},\ldots,Z_{en_e}\) are independent and identically distributed; the two environment samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) is an endogenous observed exposure; there is no randomized assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive innovation variances imply positive-definite covariance matrices; no propensity-score condition is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The nuisance is the covariance pair together with its discontinuous exact equality and sepset ledger. The procedure inverts exact Wishart covariance pivots and recomputes every compatible ledger, LDiffPC output, and direct-effect fiber inside the covariance region.

tldr: The proposal treats the complete LDiffPC equality and sepset ledger as a discontinuous nuisance rather than a selected truth. It projects an exact paired Wishart covariance region through every diff-faithful baseline-intervention completion whose typed coefficient-change DAG \(D(M)\) agrees with the partial difference graph, giving finite-sample coverage of the fixed environment-specific direct-effect triple as equality, conditional-independence, and competing-completion margins vanish. A finite semialgebraic branch representation yields a random-closed-set limit law under \(N^{-1/2}\)-local approaches to joint ledger boundaries. A same-law chain--fork family proves that noncontraction is sometimes information-theoretically necessary, while an exact \(p=3\) collider audit shows that unresolved orientation can leave \(\Psi_3\) singleton. The open question asks whether the precisely defined bounded Gaussian expected-diameter infimum is attained and whether an attaining rule has a strictly shorter honest finite-sample pullback.

project_justification.gap: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC supplies population discovery of a typed difference DAG from cross-environment regression equalities but no effect inference. StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 establishes asymptotic test inversion, structure unioning, and an explicit confidence construction for one scalar total effect under unknown single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian DAG structure; StriederDrton2023Confidence treats the same single-environment total-effect setting; WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets uses residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests in identifiable additive-error structural equation models to obtain asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and post-processed model-uncertainty effect intervals; ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection gives asymptotic screening-union coverage after ordinary conditional-independence discovery; GraduZrnicWangJordan2025ValidInference targets an effect indexed by a randomized selected graph; and GuoWuYiu2026Price gives exact selective coverage for a selected adjustment functional after Gaussian FCI with known variance. None supplies the exact paired unrestricted-covariance Wishart pivot, the two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset direct-effect fiber, exact unconditional coverage for a fixed direct-effect triple, the jointly local branch-cone boundary random-set law, or a same-law width lower bound for that fiber.
project_justification.niche: The paired Gaussian model has an exact finite-sample covariance pivot and a finite semialgebraic causal-fiber map. Together they permit unconditional inference for a fixed direct-effect triple without selecting a ledger, followed by a precise tangent-cone analysis of the resulting random set.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact uniform coverage, derives the zeroth- and first-order boundary random-set limits, gives the exact cone-aware score-image reduction on a regular singleton branch and its product-score form at ambient-interior points, and certifies an exact observational-equivalence lower bound. It leaves the genuinely nonroutine optimal-width acceptance-region problem explicit.

technical_internal_limitation: The exact covariance projection may be computationally expensive because every candidate covariance induces a fresh equality ledger and compatible-completion fiber. The proposal makes no polynomial-time claim. At boundary points with distinct elements of \(\Gamma(s_0)\), the confidence union generally has a non-singleton zeroth-order limit; Theorem 4 shows that this behavior can be unavoidable. Open-ended Question 1 asserts no convex-duality representation, least-favorable prior, attainment, strict improvement, or solution. Its possible finite-sample improvement is not a theorem.
honest_scope: The uniform coverage theorem is finite-sample and ranges over positive diff-faithful baseline-parent modular interventions with invariant Gaussian innovation variances; it assumes no known ledger, unique order, unique branch, beta-min condition, or uniform margin away from the excluded non-diff-faithful laws. The random-set limit is pointwise along \(N^{-1/2}\)-local sequences satisfying standard tangent-cone regularity and branch smoothness. The collider audit and its singleton statement concern only \(p=3\); no embedding or conclusion for \(p>3\) is claimed. The proposal does not assert the exhausted componentwise uniform-single-door necessity frontier, fixed-treewidth tractability, latent-variable robustness, optimal-width attainment, or a strictly improved pullback. On a unique relative-interior branch, Proposition 1 retains the branch tangent cone in the first-order score image; only at an ambient-interior point does it reduce to the linear image of the product of the two environment-specific score bodies, generally a Minkowski sum rather than a joint Wald ellipsoid. The BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B application is a reporting consumer, not evidence that its empirical ledger satisfies the maintained causal assumptions.
